title: No S1 rule, parameter or threshold is in force to decide what reopens the route, and no rule id is named for the record
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3.md (A2.11.2, A2.11.3.1 VR-S1-011-1 and BR-S1-011, A2.11.4.1 AC-S1-011-01); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-UNI-02, R-UNI-22, R-UNI-37, R-DEV-19, R-UNI-38); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md (E4 FEAT-VAL-11 row); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP-04 and DP-06, R9)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s8 BR5; s12.5 Workflows; s13 | APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 5 and 6; s8 BR3; s9; s13 Configuration and reference data
description: Both legacy criteria require the result to be recorded with its rule version, and no S1 rule is in force for the reconsider step: the routing logic carries universal rows that name the outcome state ROUTE_D6_REOPEN but no S1 row, no parameter and no threshold decide what counts as a change to the picture, and the S1 rule package is Phase 2. No source names the rule that maps a value, a payment or a deviation to a reopen, the parameter that says how large a change must be, or the rule id the record must carry. The step therefore reads the rule id, the rule version, the segment dimensions and the gate thresholds in force for the business date, records that version and asserts no rule id, no threshold and no parameter of its own.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.11.3.1 gives only VR-S1-011-1 (required field empty) and BR-S1-011 (no value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version), and A2.11.4.1 gives AC-S1-011-01 with 'the result is recorded with its rule version'; the routing sheet of Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 gives no S1 rule row, and its R-UNI-02, R-UNI-22 and R-UNI-37 rows move the case to ROUTE_D6_REOPEN from any active state without a threshold; R-DEV-19 gives ROUTE_D6 on a deviation re-route; TSD S1 carries no rule package and no parameter for the step.
area: Rules and reference data, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the business owner of module S1
proposed: The rule and reference-data owner publishes the S1 reconsider rule with its id, its version, its segment dimensions and its gate thresholds as a row in force of rwb-decision; until then the step reads the version in force and records it, and no threshold is built.

title: The deviation read, the rule-in-force read and the two data-product codes are not published with an operation name
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml (/cases/{caseId}/deviations and /deviations/{deviationId} as writes of module S8, /data-products/{productCode}/records, /cases/{caseId}/recommendation, /cases/{caseId}, /authorise); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2.md (T-A.1, T5.1, T5.2); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.11.2)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s12.9 Call-type summary; s13 | APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2 and 3; s12.2; s12.8; s13
description: The reconsider step consumes six rows across five owners and no source publishes four of them by name. The API Specification v4 publishes only writes on the deviations of a case, POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations with right U and PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}, both module S8, and no read of the deviations of a case; it publishes GET /data-products/{productCode}/records but names no product code for the payments of v_ace_payment or for the accepted appraisal; and it publishes no rule-in-force, segment or gate read of rwb-decision. Only GET /cases/{caseId}/recommendation, GET /cases/{caseId} and POST /authorise are published by name. The baseline and the application story therefore build against a documented use and a placeholder for the four unpublished rows and declare no path, parameter or transport for them. The deviation entity also carries a CAS Field ID range (DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045) while its operations are S8's, which no source reconciles.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack give S1 three REST operations, no table, no event, no job and one workflow, and name no consumed operation; the API Specification v4 gives x-module S8 and x-capability Case record U on POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations, and no GET on that path; it gives /data-products/{productCode}/records with a productCode parameter and no list of codes; TSD S1 T5.2 names P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 as published Java interfaces with no operation name and does not name S8; the Logical Data Model v8 places deviation under the CAS Field IDs with source Workbench.
owner_role: S8 rwb-deviation owner, P7 rwb-decision owner and P1 rwb-source-data owner with the S1 service owner
proposed: Each owner publishes the read operation, its parameters and, for the data products, its product codes; until then the clients and their fakes are built from the documented use and the placeholder, and a published name replaces it in a minor contract version with no behaviour change.

title: The value trigger is declared against FEAT-VAL-07 while the value itself is accepted in FEAT-VAL-04, and no source says whether a new value reopens on its own
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md (E4 FEAT-VAL-04, FEAT-VAL-07 and FEAT-VAL-11 rows); Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3.md (A2.11.2 prerequisites FEAT-VAL-07, A2.4 accept the appraisal value); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-011 Data table, which lists no appraisal value)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s11 Data | APP s2; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 1 and 3; s11 Data; s19
description: FEAT-VAL-11 declares FEAT-VAL-07 as its prerequisite, and the page it depends on is the recommendation, while the value that changes the picture is accepted in FEAT-VAL-04, which fixes the band the route decision runs on. The legacy Data table of the key lists the deviation, the payment, the decision record and the rule row and no appraisal value at all. No source says whether a newly accepted value reopens the route decision on its own or only once the recommendation is recomputed, nor which of the two features owns the trigger. The stories read the accepted appraisal value on the rwb-source-data data product and treat the reopen as the step that restarts the route decision from the expected return and the recommendation, without claiming either feature's behaviour.
evidence: The Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 gives FEAT-VAL-04 'Lets the case owner accept the value, which fixes the band the route decision runs on', FEAT-VAL-07 'Runs the route agent, which recommends a route', and FEAT-VAL-11 'Reopens the route decision when a value, a payment or a deviation changes the picture' with 'Depends on FEAT-VAL-07'; FSD S1 A2.11.2 gives FEAT-VAL-07 as the prerequisite and A2.11.3.2 lists the appraisal fields of v_ace_valuation; the legacy Data table of RWB-E4-011 lists deviation, v_ace_payment, decision_log_entry and rule_row only.
owner_role: The business owner of module S1 with the S1 service owner
proposed: The module owner confirms the trigger set of the reopen; until then the step accepts the accepted value of FEAT-VAL-04 as one of the three kinds of new information and reports the reopen to the route decision, which then runs FEAT-VAL-05 and FEAT-VAL-07 again.

title: No table or element is fixed for the earlier route decision and the versions it was taken under, which the reopen must compare against and supersede
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1: no table); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2.md (T3.1 valuation and score, T3.3 relationships); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-011 Data table: decision_log_entry DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-38, R-UNI-24)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s18 Traceability | APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 8 and 10; s8 BR4; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s13
description: The reopen supersedes an earlier decision and R-UNI-38 keeps an open case on the version it was decided under, so the step must read the earlier decision, its rule version and its model version and name it in the new record. The Ownership Map gives S1 no table, TSD S1 T3.1 declares valuation and score and no route-decision object, and the legacy Data table names decision_log_entry as a P7 row. No source fixes whether the earlier decision is read from the local decision record, from the rwb-decision ledger or from a store of this service, nor which of them the reopen compares against. Neither story declares a table or a column of its own and the earlier decision is referenced by its record.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack list no table under S1; TSD S1 T3.1 lists valuation (NEW) and score (REUSE ACE) only; TSD S1 T3.3 gives no decision relationship; the legacy Data table lists decision_log_entry with DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018; R-UNI-38 keeps an open case on the version it was decided under and R-UNI-24 requires a correcting entry to name the original.
area: Data model and ownership, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P7 rwb-decision owner and the data steward
proposed: The data owner names the store of the earlier decision and its versions; if it is a table, the DB story of this service creates it in its own Flyway sequence and the writer fills it, and until then the local decision record holds the reopen and the earlier decision reference.

title: No published element carries the change that caused a reopen on the route operation, and no operation of this service returns a reopen
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml (RouteRequest, Approval, Recommendation, /cases/{caseId}/route); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2.md (T-A.1, T-A.2); Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3.md (A2.11.4.1)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s7 C2 and C4; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.8 Contract fakes | APP s4 Flow steps 1, 8 and 11; s12.1; s12.2
description: The legacy criterion reopens the route decision and records the result with its rule version, but the published RouteRequest carries only route, overrideReasonCode and note, and Approval carries only id, caseId, decision, preparedBy, level, amount and status. No element names the new information that caused the reopen, the segment before and after, the outcome state or the earlier decision, and no operation of S1 returns a reopen. No source says whether the reopen should be a distinct submission on the same operation, a new operation, or a fact recorded and read only on the decision row and the recommendation read. The baseline therefore declares the route operation as published, declares the reopen element by reference to the record and the recommendation row, and asserts no element name on RouteRequest or Approval.
evidence: The API Specification v4 publishes RouteRequest with route, overrideReasonCode and note and Approval with id, caseId, decision, preparedBy, level, amount and status, and Recommendation with decision, recommended, reasons, expectedReturnByRoute, ruleVersion and agentVersion; TSD S1 T-A.2 gives API-S1-001 as 'Request RouteRequest, Response Approval' with no element list; FSD S1 A2.11.4.1 states only that the result is recorded with its rule version.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P7 rwb-decision owner
proposed: If an element is required on the answer, it is added as an optional element in a minor version with its fake; until then the reopen is carried by the reason code and the note of the submission and by the record, and no element is invented.

title: No event, timer or subscription notifies a payment, an appraisal acceptance or a deviation change to this service, and S1 owns no job and no event
source: Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3.md (A2.11.2 step 1 actor, A2.11.4.4 system background events); _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2.md (T5.3 events: None)
section: CON s12.4 Events consumed; s12.6 Schedules | APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 1; s12.4 Events consumed; s12.6 Schedules
description: The legacy story reopens the route decision when a value, a payment or a deviation changes the picture, and FSD S1 A2.11 declares no background event and drives the feature from the case owner on the screen. The ownership rows give S1 no job and no event and TSD S1 T5.3 is 'None', so no subscription and no Schedule exists to learn of a payment, an appraisal acceptance or a deviation change, and no source names the event that would carry one. The reopen is therefore command-driven from the screen and the step reads the three kinds of new information when it runs; a change notification would be a new interface of this service with its own contract row.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.11.2 gives the actor of step 1 as 'Case owner' and A2.11.4.4 gives the row 'None, No background event'; the ownership rows of the context pack give S1 no event and no job and one workflow, RouteDecisionWorkflow; TSD S1 T5.3 is the row 'None'; the API Specification v4 publishes no subscription of S1.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P8 rwb-payment, P1 rwb-source-data and S8 rwb-deviation owners
proposed: If the business needs the reopen without an officer action, the owners publish a change event or the service owner adds a Temporal Schedule covering the business date; until then the reopen is submitted from SCR-13 and the step reads the facts when it runs.
